claims.statement: Arrow keys resize by a declared step, Shift coarsens it, Home and End reach the bounds, PageUp and PageDown move between snap points, and Enter restores the default.
Every size reachable by dragging is reachable from the keyboard, because both paths commit through the same clamped setter.
The drag gesture is not the only way to resize; the separator is focusable and fully operable by key.
aria-valuetext carries a sentence naming the panel and its size, so the value is announced as meaning rather than as a bare number, and changes wording when snapped or collapsed.
The separator takes focus and paints a visible ring plus an emphasised seam; it never takes focus without being operable.
Under prefers-reduced-motion the seam changes colour without the thickness transition.
Resizing writes a custom property that drives a logical size; no transition is applied to the panel dimension, so a drag never animates layout.
At every reachable size, including the declared minimum, the panel reflows without introducing horizontal document overflow.
The affordance is a painted bar rather than a fill on the hit area, so it survives forced-colors discarding author backgrounds.

The pointer drag path is NOT covered by these stories. The story runner supports settle, click, key, type and blur interactions and has no pointer-drag primitive, so pointer coverage lives in the hook's unit tests and in browser captures until a pointerDrag interaction kind exists.

component.purpose: The drag affordance for a resizable region, operable and perceivable without a pointer.
component.title: Resize Handle

states.description: A vertical seam at rest between a panel and a workspace.
The inline axis: a vertical separator between two columns.
The block axis: a horizontal separator between two stacked regions.
Arrow keys resize in declared pixel steps with no pointer involved.
Driven to the declared floor; content stays legible and the value never goes lower.
Settled on a declared snap point, with the announcement saying so.
Below the collapse threshold; the handle remains the way back out.
Right-to-left, where the growth direction is the mirror of the physical one.
System high contrast, where author background colors are discarded.
